title: Mentioning the goal of expanding or developing the business may predict slower funding for female borrowers.
Pitches from women that explicitly state their marital status or widowhood tend to fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention specific assets like home ownership or geographic distance from cities may fund faster.
Quantifying professional experience or tenure in a field accelerates the funding process for both men and women.
Female borrowers who emphasize sustaining their business through their own efforts may fund more slowly.
Pitches from women that include a concrete count of children tend to accelerate the funding process.
Specifying the exact number of children may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Pitches from women that specify large quantities of assets or long years of experience tend to decelerate funding.
Mentioning marital status or the presence of children may predict slower funding for women.
Female borrowers who explicitly mention the use of past loans may fund more slowly.
Mentioning specific institutional or brand names predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning environmental protection predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention dreams or future aspirations predict slower funding.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their age fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention children's education or food security fund faster.
Female borrowers who describe themselves as hardworking fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention owning or aspiring to own property fund faster.
